insights.title: Demand outlook shifts from recovery to caution
insights.summary: On the Q4 2025 call, management called Q1 the low point for underlying demand, with improvement through 2026. On the Q1 2026 call, it said Q1 sell-through and Q2 sell-through expectations were 10% to 15% below its prior view, blaming weather and TPO financing. On the Q2 2026 call, it reported US sell-through down 34% year on year and cited higher interest rates. It also guided Q3 with a deliberate under-shipment, citing cautious distributors.
insights.uw_relevance: The 'low point' framing from the first call was followed by a guidance reset and then explicit caution about macro and rates. Underwriters can weigh how reliable management's demand forecasts have been, and the risk of further estimate misses.

evidence.snippet: We continue to believe Q1 marks the low point for underlying demand with improvement expected through 2026, particularly in the second half.

evidence.snippet: Our Q2 26 sell-through declined 34% as compared to 1 year ago, Q2 25, reflecting continued pressure from higher interest rates and the transition following the expiration of the 25B tax credit.

insights.title: TPO financing and tax equity strain emerges
insights.summary: In the Q4 2025 call, management stressed that Enphase can support all major TPOs. By the Q1 2026 call, it cited TPO financing challenges, tax equity pauses and installer bankruptcies as headwinds. In the Q2 2026 call, it said tax equity is tight and that Treasury guidance has limited visibility. It described its response as taking 'matters into our own hands' through prepaid leases and new products.
insights.uw_relevance: Enphase's near-term US residential and safe harbor revenue depends on third-party owners whose funding is now described as constrained. This is counterparty and demand-concentration risk that was absent from the earlier call.
